verdicts.quote: If any problem is found in the file, no user from the file is created, and the user list is exactly as before.
the admin sees one entry per problem row (more if a row has several problems), each containing the line number and a description of the problem
every row after the first is reported as a problem on its line, saying the address repeats ... A row whose address already belongs to a user is reported as a problem on its line
Every user created by an import has no admin rights, whatever the file contains; the file has no way to grant them.
A signed-in user without admin rights who sends an upload is refused with a message that they lack permission
verdicts.missing: Whether import is a distinct permission from creating a single user, or simply implied by admin/single-create rights.

verdicts.quote: The first line of the file names the columns. ... If the header lacks `email` or `name`, the admin sees a message naming each missing column ... A file with extra columns is accepted
A value in double quotes may contain commas, line breaks ... LF and ... CRLF create the same users ... with or without a leading byte-order mark, is read correctly
An imported user gets the same defaults, the same notifications or invitations ... If any problem is found in the file, no user from the file is created
verdicts.missing: Whether invitations/notifications are sent only after the whole import commits, so no mail goes out for rows of a file that is later refused or interrupted.

verdicts.quote: a file with 1,001 is refused with a message that states the limit of 1,000 ... one of 1,048,577 bytes is refused with a message that states the limit
An empty file, or one with only a header line (and blank lines), is refused with a message saying there are no users to import
They see that nothing was created and that each row's address already belongs to a user. No user is duplicated or changed.
From submit to seeing the result, a valid 1,000-row file takes at most 60 seconds on an ordinary deployment.
verdicts.missing: Whether processing runs inline in the request or in the background, and how the admin learns it finished if they leave the page.

verdicts.quote: An imported user gets the same defaults, the same notifications or invitations ... as a user an admin creates individually
verdicts.missing: Whether up to 1,000 invitations go out at once and any pacing or throttling of that mail.

verdicts.quote: An imported user gets the same defaults, the same notifications or invitations, and the same way of first signing in as a user an admin creates individually
They correct the file and submit it again; this time all rows are created and the count is shown.
verdicts.missing: Whether a running import can be cancelled; retry is only by resubmitting the whole corrected file.

verdicts.quote: a valid 1,000-row file takes at most 60 seconds on an ordinary deployment
verdicts.missing: Whether and how progress is shown to the admin while the import runs.

verdicts.quote: Creating one user by hand, editing a user and viewing the list behave as they did before ... every user who existed before it has the same name, email, rights and state as before.
one with 255 is reported as a problem on its line naming the email field ... one with 101 is reported as a problem on its line, naming the name field
verdicts.missing: Handling of values that would become spreadsheet formulas (e.g. leading =, +, -, @) when shown or exported.
